newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia to spend $235 million on new roads.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia to spend $235 million on new roads.

text.p: Ethiopia is to spend $235 million in the next five years on building a new rural road network and repairing existing ones, a senior government official said on Tuesday.

Tesfa-Mikeal Nahusenaye, general manager of the Ethiopian Road Authority, told reporters the authority would build a new rural road netowork of around 5,000 km (3,100 miles) and repair 10,000 km (6,200 miles) of existing highways.
Tesfa-Mikeal said his organisation had been restructured to meet the project without fail but offered no further details.
He said the cost of the project would be met by foreign donors and the government. He did not say in what proportion.
Tesfa-Mikeal said the authority would impose road tolls on users to help maintain roads and safeguard against poor repair. He did not say when that would be or how much the fee would be.
